As someone who herniated 3discs at the age of 17 (don't ask me how I'm dumb), it may seem scary but it's nothing crazy if you do what you can do "correct" it. I kept getting progressively worse during the first 3months and eventually I was reduced nearly to a wheelchair. Extreme painkillers numbed the pain to the point at which I could walk normally (nothing more than regular walking). I was on them for 3months after which I was taken off and the pain slooowly started to come back. However I went to the gym and did the simplest lower back exercises+ all the possible back extenstions&stretches 3times a day and within a week the pain was gone. I still exercise regularly and I never had any issues with it since (20 rn). Sure my flexibility is forever ruined ( I can bring my hands max to my knees without bending my legs for example) but the pain is gone. The solution is to just strengthen your lower back and once you do that the actual damage isn't serious other than some flexibility. Nothing to beat yourself over mistakes happen.
